memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then she said, 'Here is Bilhah, my servant. Sleep with her so that she can bear children for me and I too can build a family through her.' So she gave him her servant Bilhah as a wife. Jacob slept with her, and she became pregnant and bore him a son. Then Rachel said, 'God has vindicated me; he has listened to my plea and given me a son.' Because of this she named him Dan. Rachel's servant Bilhah conceived again and bore Jacob a second son. Then Rachel said, 'I have had a great struggle with my sister, and I have won.' So she named him Naphtali." - Gen 30:3-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Desperate for children, Rachel gives her servant Bilhah to Jacob so she can have sons "through her." Two sons are born this way, and Rachel names the second Naphtali, saying, "I have had a great struggle with my sister, and I have won." Her words say it all: this has become a contest, sister against sister, and children have become the trophies.

How sad this is. What should have been a home of love has become a battlefield of rivalry. And notice the cost — Bilhah is handed over as little more than a means to an end. When we are consumed by competition, people get used and relationships get damaged.

The Bible records all of this without approving of it. God's design for the family was never this tangle of rivalry and using people (Gen 2:24). What we see here is the bitter fruit of hearts driven by envy and the need to "win."

Comparison and competition steal our joy and poison our love. There is no real winner in a contest to outdo those closest to us. The way of Christ is different — "in humility value others above yourselves" (Phil 2:3). Instead of striving to win against others, we are called to love them. Ask God to free you from the exhausting need to compete and compare.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where has comparison turned a relationship into a competition?
2. Am I using people or truly loving them?
3. How would valuing others above myself change my relationships?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, free me from the exhausting need to compete and compare. Heal the rivalries in my heart, and teach me to love others rather than to win against them. Amen.
